Formerly part of the Rockingham Estate laid out by the King family, it is open to the public.


== History ==
Rockingham House had burned down in a fire started by an electrical fault in 1957.  The house had been designed by John Nash around 1810.
What remained of the estate was sold by Sir Cecil Stafford-King-Harman, to the Irish Land Commission in May 1959. The Land Commission officially took control of the estate in November 1959.
After the ruins of the house were demolished in 1971, the 150 ft (45.72 m) Moylurg Viewing Tower was built on the site in 1973, and designed in the Brutalist architecture style by Irish architect by James Fehily of Fehily and Associates The servant's tunnels still exist, with one entrance near the tower.


== Park ==
The part of the estate that later became Lough Key Forest Park was handed over by the Land Commission to the Forestry Commission around 1972. In 1988, the Forestry Commission became Coillte, a State company. Lough Key Forest Park has been owned and run by Coillte since that time.
